## Overview

-   How to build a scatterplot
-   How to run a correlation analysis and interpret the result

::: notes
In this video I'll walk you through how to build a scatterplot in R and how to conduct a correlation analysis and interpret the result.
:::

## Step 1: Setup - load libraries

```{r}
#| label: load_libraries
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: true
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(easystats)
```

1.  [The `here` package helps with finding your files]{style="color: grey;"}
2.  [The `tidyverse` is a set of packages that handles almost everything you need to do with data]{style="color: grey;"}
3.  `easystats` is a set of packages that handles many statistical analyses; including the function that we need to run correlation analysis

## Step 2: Reading in the data

```{r}
#| label: read_data
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: true
data_mw_subscales <- read_csv(here("PSYC4141/files/week3", "data_bmw3_subscales.csv"))
```

1. `read_csv` reads in data; we need to tell R where the file is and what it is called

`<-` is an assignment arrow, telling R that we want to put the data in an object (or dataframe) called `data_mw_subscales`


## Step 3a: Build a scatterplot

::: panel-tabset

### Code

```{r}
#| label: scatterplot_code
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: true
ggplot(data = data_mw_subscales, mapping = aes(x = BMW3_UN, y= BMW3_ME)) +
  geom_point()
```
1. We use `ggplot()` to tell R what data to plot and which variables to use
2. We use `geom_point()` to tell R that we want a scatterplot

### Plot

```{r}
#| label: scatterplot_output
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| fig-width: 5
library (here)
library(tidyverse)

data_mw_subscales <- read_csv(here("PSYC4141/files/week3", "data_bmw3_subscales.csv"))

ggplot(data = data_mw_subscales, mapping = aes(x = BMW3_UN, y= BMW3_ME)) +
  geom_point() 
```

:::

## Step 3b: Add a line of best fit

::: panel-tabset

### Code

```{r}
#| label: scatterplot_withline_code
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: true

ggplot(data = data_mw_subscales, mapping = aes(x = BMW3_UN, y= BMW3_ME)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE)
```

3. We use `geom_smooth()`, with the `method = "lm"` to add a line of best fit; `se` refers to the standard error around the line

### Plot

```{r}
#| label: scatterplot_withline_output
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| fig-width: 5

ggplot(data = data_mw_subscales, mapping = aes(x = BMW3_UN, y= BMW3_ME)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE)
```

:::

## Step 3c: Tidy up the scatterplot

::: panel-tabset

### Code

```{r}
#| label: scatterplot_tidy_code
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: true

ggplot(data = data_mw_subscales, mapping = aes(x = BMW3_UN, y= BMW3_ME)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Unintentional mind wandering", y = "Meta-awareness of mind wandering")
```

4. We use `theme_bw()` to change the background
5. We use `labs()` to add informative titles to the axes

### Plot

```{r}
#| label: scatterplot_tidy_output
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| fig-width: 5

ggplot(data = data_mw_subscales, mapping = aes(x = BMW3_UN, y= BMW3_ME)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Unintentional mind wandering", y = "Meta-awareness of mind wandering")
```

:::

## Step 4: Correlation analysis

::: panel-tabset

### Code

```{r}
#| label: correlation_code
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: true

correlation(data = data_mw_subscales,
            select = c("BMW3_UN", "BMW3_ME"),
            method = "pearson",
            p_adjust = "none")
```

::: {style="font-size: 0.7em"}
1. We use the `correlation()` function and tell R what data to use
2. We specify the variables we want to correlate using `select()`
3. We specify which method to use; `"pearson"` is the default
4. [We'll talk about that in a couple of weeks]{style="color: grey;"}
:::

### Output

```{r}
#| label: correlation_output
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

library (easystats)

correlation(data = data_mw_subscales,
            select = c("BMW3_UN", "BMW3_ME"),
            method = "pearson",
            p_adjust = "none")
```

:::
